h1:
Where to Stay in Krabi?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Krabi hotels across every budget — from 5-star beachfront pavilions on Railay down to Ao Nang dorms from ฿150/night. Covering the main areas: Railay, Ao Nang, Noppharat Thara, Klong Muang–Tubkaak, Koh Lanta and Krabi Town. From roughly ฿150–16,000/night.
heroStats: 🏖️ 6 key areas (Railay·Ao Nang·Noppharat Thara·Klong Muang-Tubkaak·Koh Lanta·Town)
introH2: 🏖️ Why does choosing the right area in Krabi matter so much?
introHtml: Krabi isn't a single beach — each area has a completely different vibe. Railay is famous for its limestone cliffs and clear water, but it's reachable only by boat (no road in). Ao Nang is the tourist hub: restaurants, shops, the island-hopping pier and accommodation at every price point. Noppharat Thara sits just past Ao Nang, quieter and more family-friendly. Klong Muang–Tubkaak to the north is a calm resort zone. Koh Lanta needs a boat or car ferry and suits travellers who want to escape the crowds. And Krabi Town isn't on the beach but is cheap and well-connected. Many people book without checking the area, then lose hours shuttling back and forth by road or boat. This guide rounds up 12 Krabi hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Krabi has no metro. Getting around means rental car, scooter, taxi, songthaew, or longtail/speedboat (for Railay and the islands). From Krabi Airport (KBV) it's about 30–40 min to Ao Nang, 20 min to town, and 40–50 min to Klong Muang–Tubkaak. Railay has no road access — you take a longtail from Ao Nang or town (around 10–15 min). Koh Lanta needs a boat or car ferry, roughly 1.5–2 hours from the airport. The areas in this guide: Railay — limestone cliffs, clear water, boat-only · Ao Nang — the hub, restaurants and piers · Noppharat Thara — quieter, family-friendly · Klong Muang–Tubkaak — calm resort zone · Koh Lanta — escape the crowds · Krabi Town — cheap and well-connected.

entries.name: Rayavadee
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phranang Peninsula · Railay Beach · boat access only
tags: 🏅 The Leading Hotels of the World
entries.storyHtml: The top luxury score in this guide at 9.4 — Rayavadee is a 5-star resort on the Phranang Peninsula where rooms are round, two-storey pavilions scattered through coconut groves beside Railay Beach. The resort is ringed by limestone cliffs and sits on three beaches, reachable only by boat, so it feels very private. Real guest reviews praise the postcard setting and attentive service, but note the high prices and limited dining options nearby since everything requires a boat trip.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The boat transfer leaves from Ao Nang / Ao Phranang — check schedules and sea conditions during monsoon season. The entry-level Deluxe Pavilion is already beautiful and spacious; only upgrade to a Hydro Pool Pavilion if you want a private pool.
pros: Top luxury score 9.4 from 599 reviews — attentive service
Pavilions in coconut groves by Railay-Phranang, postcard-perfect
Sits on three beaches, ringed by limestone cliffs, very private
Boat-access only — a calm escape from the crowds
cons: Highest price in the guide — best for a special trip or honeymoon
Everything is a boat ride away; limited dining nearby

entries.name: Panan Krabi Resort
entries.badge: 💬 Heavily reviewed · best Ao Nang value
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Ao Nang · walk to beach & restaurants
entries.storyHtml: Panan is a 4-star boutique resort in central Ao Nang with a strong 9.1 from a hefty 614 reviews. You can walk to Ao Nang Beach, the restaurants and the island-hopping pier. Entry-level rooms have private balconies, and there are Pool Access rooms you can step straight into the pool from. Real guest reviews praise the value and the do-everything-on-foot location — ideal if you want a 4-star base in the centre without paying premium prices.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entry-level Deluxe is great value if location is your priority. Travelling as a family? Look at the Family Two-Bedroom Suite to bring the per-person cost down.
pros: 9.1 from a large 614 reviews — consistent and trustworthy
Central Ao Nang — walk to the beach, restaurants and pier
Pool Access rooms let you step into the pool from your balcony
Best value for a 4-star in the heart of Ao Nang
cons: In the heart of the tourist strip — busy and lively in high season
Not a step-onto-the-sand resort; you walk out to the beach

entries.name: The Tubkaak Krabi Boutique Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tubkaak Beach · Klong Muang · island views
tags: 🏝️ Views of Hong Island & the northern sea
entries.storyHtml: The Tubkaak is a 5-star boutique beach resort on Tubkaak–Klong Muang beach in northern Krabi, scoring 9.1. The draw is the quiet private beach with views of Hong Island and the northern sea. Entry-level rooms are a generous 45 sqm, and there are pool villas for honeymooners. Real guest reviews praise the calm and the warm service, but flag that it's far from Ao Nang and dining outside the resort is limited.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: This spot is all about quiet relaxation — factor in driving time if you want to be in Ao Nang every day. The Garden Room is already roomy and lovely; only step up to a pool villa if you want a private pool.
pros: 5-star boutique on quiet, private Tubkaak Beach
Views of Hong Island and the northern sea — gorgeous at sunset
Spacious 45 sqm entry rooms, plus pool villas
Warm service; ideal for couples escaping the bustle
cons: Far from Ao Nang — town outings mean a fair drive
Limited dining outside the resort due to the quiet location

entries.name: Sand Sea Resort
tags: 🌅 Wake up and walk onto the sand
entries.addr: 39 Moo 2, Railay West Beach, Ao Nang, Mueang Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Sand Sea is a 4-star resort right on Railay West Beach from just ฿2,600, scoring 9.1 from 411 reviews. The appeal is the location — you wake up and walk straight onto Railay Beach without paying Rayavadee prices. Rooms are garden bungalows and villas. Real guest reviews praise the beachfront setting and leafy grounds, but note that Railay is boat-only and food on the beach costs more than in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Railay has few ATMs and convenience stores — bring enough cash. Book your longtail from Ao Nang and allow time at low tide, when boats sometimes can't reach the sand and you wade in.
pros: Right on Railay West Beach — walk onto the sand each morning
9.1 from 411 reviews at a from-price of just ฿2,600
Garden bungalows and villas — leafy and private
Railay access at a far lower price than the luxury resorts
cons: Railay is boat-only; food on the beach is pricier
At low tide boats may not reach the sand — you wade ashore

entries.name: Nakamanda Resort & Spa
entries.badge: 💆 Spa & villas on Klong Muang Beach
entries.addr: 126 Moo 3, Klong Muang, Nong Thale, Mueang Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Nakamanda is a 5-star boutique beach resort on Klong Muang Beach built around calm villa living and a spa, scoring 9.0. The villas mix Lanna and tropical styling, from garden views up to Jacuzzi and sea-view pool villas. Real guest reviews praise the privacy and the spa; the review count is still modest (65) but the score is consistent. A good pick for couples who want a luxury beachfront resort for less than Rayavadee or Tubkaak.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Klong Muang is a quiet beach with no nightlife — have a car to pop over to Ao Nang. The Sala Villa Sea View costs only a little more but gives you a morning sea view.
pros: 5-star boutique on Klong Muang Beach — calm and private
Well-regarded spa, consistently praised in real reviews
Villa choice from garden views to Jacuzzi/sea-view pool villas
Beachfront luxury below Krabi's top-tier resort prices
cons: Modest review count (65) compared with others here
Klong Muang is quiet with no nightlife — a car helps

entries.name: Nomads Ao Nang
entries.storyHtml: Nomads Ao Nang is the most-reviewed property in this guide — over 3,342 reviews, a high 9.6 score, and the cheapest at just ฿150. It's all about the social scene: activities, parties and group island trips make it dead easy to meet fellow travellers. AC dorms have curtained bunks with lights, plugs and lockers. It's ages 18–35 only. Real guest reviews love the atmosphere and activities — but it's clearly not for anyone wanting quiet or travelling as a family.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Book here if you want to meet people and party. If you want to actually sleep, pick the 6-bed ensuite dorm, or switch to Pak-Up for a mellower vibe.
pros: Most reviewed in the guide at 3,342 · high 9.6 score
Cheapest at ฿150 — top value for backpackers
Strong social scene: activities, parties, group island trips
AC dorms with curtained bunks, lights, plugs, lockers · central Ao Nang
cons: It's a party hostel — loud, not for quiet seekers
Ages 18–35 only; not suitable for families

entries.name: Ananta Burin Resort
entries.storyHtml: Ananta Burin is a 4-star family resort in the Noppharat Thara–Ao Nang area with its own water park, scoring 8.9 from 279 reviews. The draw is the water park and multiple pools that keep kids busy all day, plus large family rooms — all from just ฿1,500. Real guest reviews call it excellent value for families with young children. Best for those who want in-resort fun for the kids more than a step-onto-the-sand location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The resort isn't on the beach — there's a shuttle to Noppharat Thara / Ao Nang, so check the timetable. Travelling as a group? The Triple Family or Two-Bedroom rooms work out cheaper.
pros: Water park and multiple pools — kids stay busy all day
Large family rooms from just ฿1,500
Excellent value for families with young children
Noppharat Thara–Ao Nang area, easy to reach town
cons: Not on the beach — you use the shuttle to get there
Family-focused; pools and water park get busy in high season

entries.name: Avani+ Koh Lanta Krabi Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Klong Khong / north of Koh Lanta
tags: 🏝️ On Koh Lanta, away from the crowds
entries.storyHtml: Avani+ Koh Lanta is a 4-star beachfront boutique resort on Koh Lanta, part of Avani / Minor Hotels, scoring 8.8 from 384 reviews. The appeal is being on Koh Lanta — far quieter than the Ao Nang side — ideal for escaping the crowds. Entry rooms are a generous 50 sqm and there are Pool Access rooms. Real guest reviews praise the calm and the room size, but note that getting to Koh Lanta takes a while and involves a boat or car ferry.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Koh Lanta is far out — plan several nights to make the trip worthwhile. In low season (May–Oct) some island services close, so check before you book.
pros: On Koh Lanta — quiet, away from the Ao Nang crowds
Beachfront setting, private feel
Spacious 50 sqm entry rooms, plus Pool Access options
Avani / Minor Hotels — reliable service standards
cons: Getting to Koh Lanta takes a while — boat or car ferry
Some island services close in low season — check first

entries.name: Pak-Up Hostel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Krabi Town · Utarakit Rd, Pak Nam
tags: 🚍 In town, near pier & bus terminal
entries.addr: 87 Utarakit Road, Pak Nam, Mueang Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Pak-Up is a social hostel in Krabi Town with dorms from just ฿270 and an 8.8 score. It's on Utarakit Road in the centre, near the pier, bus terminal and cheap eats, making onward travel to the islands or Ao Nang easy. Dorms have curtained wooden bunks, AC and lockers, and there's a female-only dorm. Real guest reviews praise the location and a social vibe that's mellower than a party hostel — great for backpackers using town as a base.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's in town, not on the beach — use it as a base for day boats/buses out to Ao Nang and Railay. There's a bar downstairs that can get noisy at night; ask for an upper bunk if you want quiet.
pros: Dorms from ฿270 in town — great value for backpackers
Central — near the pier, bus terminal and cheap restaurants
Curtained wooden bunks, AC, lockers · female dorm available
Mellower social vibe than a party hostel — easy to meet people
cons: In town, not on the beach — you boat/bus out to swim
Bar downstairs can be noisy at night

entries.name: Aonang Cliff Beach Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Ao Nang · hillside, sea views
entries.storyHtml: Aonang Cliff is a hillside resort in central Ao Nang whose signature is a rooftop infinity pool with Andaman sea views, scoring 8.5 from 173 reviews. Entry rooms are a generous 40 sqm, with sea-view options. The central location means you can walk to restaurants and the beach. Real guest reviews praise the rooftop pool views and the room size, but note the hillside means a climb and that some rooms are starting to show their age.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Head up for rooftop-pool photos at sunset — it's best then. The entry Superior has a limited view; if views matter, step up to a Sea View.
pros: Rooftop infinity pool with Andaman sea views — a standout
Hillside in central Ao Nang — walk to restaurants and beach
Roomy 40 sqm entry rooms with sea-view options
From ฿2,000 for a central Ao Nang location
cons: Hillside means climbing — not ideal for limited mobility
Some rooms are dated — ask for a renovated one

entries.name: GLOW Ao Nang Krabi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Nang · ~10 min walk to beach
entries.addr: 199/46 Soi 8, Moo 3, Ao Nang, Mueang Krabi
entries.storyHtml: GLOW Ao Nang is a 3-star value hotel in Ao Nang with a hefty 1,158 reviews, scoring 8.3. From just ฿1,000 you get a pool and family rooms, with Ao Nang Beach about a 10-minute walk away. Real guest reviews praise the value and location, but flag that some entry-level Standard rooms are stair-access with no lift — which is why it lands near the back of the guide. A solid pick for budget travellers who still want a hotel with a pool in Ao Nang.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Superior or above — they're newer and avoid the stair climb. The beach is about a 10-minute walk; plan around the midday heat.
pros: Heavily reviewed 1,158 · from just ฿1,000
Has a pool and family rooms on a budget
Ao Nang location, ~10-minute walk to the beach
Great for budget travellers who still want a pool
cons: Some entry Standard rooms are stair-access with no lift
It's a value hotel — basic amenities

entries.name: Krabi Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Nang · private beach at the quiet end
entries.storyHtml: Krabi Resort is a 4-star resort on a private beach at the quiet end of Ao Nang, scoring 7.9 from 176 reviews — the lowest in this guide. The appeal is the leafy beachfront setting, calmer than central Ao Nang, plus Pool Access rooms and a Beachfront Pool Villa. Real guest reviews praise the beachfront location and spacious grounds, but flag that some rooms and facilities are dated and due a refurbishment — hence its place at the back. Best for those who weigh a beachfront location over newness.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Luxury Grand room or above — newer and bigger than the entry Deluxe. Choose this if private beachfront is the priority; for newer rooms, compare Panan or Aonang Cliff.
pros: Private beach at the quiet end of Ao Nang
Leafy garden resort by the sea, spacious grounds
Pool Access rooms and a Beachfront Pool Villa
Best for those who prioritise a beachfront location
cons: Lowest score in the guide at 7.9 — some rooms are dated
Parts of the facilities are due a refurbishment

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Krabi hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Krabi for tourists?
faq.a: It depends on your style. Ao Nang is the hub with restaurants, the pier and accommodation at every tier — the most convenient base (Panan, Aonang Cliff, GLOW, Nomads). Railay Beach is postcard-pretty but boat-only (Rayavadee, Sand Sea). Klong Muang–Tubkaak is a calm resort zone (The Tubkaak, Nakamanda). Koh Lanta suits those escaping the crowds (Avani+). Krabi Town is cheap and well-connected (Pak-Up).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Krabi hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: dorms and hostels from about ฿150–320/night; mid-range and 4-star hotels and resorts around ฿1,000–4,800; 5-star beachfront resorts and pool villas from about ฿6,000–16,000+. All figures are approximate standard-room starting rates; High Season (Nov–Apr) runs much higher.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Railay Beach, and is staying there worth it?
faq.a: Railay has no road in — you take a longtail from Ao Nang or town, around 10–15 minutes. If your trip is about rock climbing, kayaking and clear water, staying on Railay (e.g. Sand Sea or Rayavadee) is worth it because you wake up on the sand. But food and shops on Railay are limited and cost more than in town, so bring enough cash and essentials.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Krabi hotel?
faq.a: On weekdays outside peak season, 2–4 weeks ahead is enough. But in High Season (November–April), especially New Year and Songkran, the best rooms and beachfront resorts fill fast — book 1–2 months ahead. During the monsoon (May–Oct) prices drop, but island boats may be cancelled on some days.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get around Krabi's beaches and islands?
faq.a: Krabi has no metro. Getting around means rental car, scooter, taxi, songthaew and longtail/speedboat. From the airport it's about 30–40 min to Ao Nang. Railay needs a boat from Ao Nang or town; Koh Lanta needs a boat or car ferry, roughly 1.5–2 hours. If you plan to visit several beaches, having a car or scooter is more convenient and cheaper.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Krabi hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so open and compare all three before every booking — each review page in this guide has full price-comparison links, which can save hundreds to thousands of baht per night at peak times.
